title: Tracking Down Chimeric Assemblies In The TrackIt DNA Ladder Using Nanopore Sequencing
author: Eccles, David Andrew
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0
materials: called_2023-Oct-12_DNA-Ladder-1kbplus_duplex.bam - duplex called reads [October 12, 2023], called using dorado v4.0 with the 2023-09-22 bacterial methylation model sequence_QC_2023-Oct-12_DNA-Ladder-1kbplus.pdf - sequence length / quality QC plots LAST_2023-Oct-12_DNA-Ladder-1kbplus_reads_vs_reference.tar.gz - Alignment summary statistics from LAST mapping of reads to their associated reference lengths_summary_2023-Oct-12_DNA-Ladder-1kbplus.txt - Length / QC summary statistics ladder_seqs.fa - assembled DNA ladder sequences, based on simplex reads Methods Sample preparation Preparation of DNA for sequencing was carried out following the ONT Ligation Sequencing DNA V14 (SQK-LSK114) protocol, with modifications to exclude DNA repair, and keeping the sample in the same 1.5ml tube to reduce sample loss. Tris-buffered Saline (TBS) buffer preparation 1M stock of NaCl was made by adding 2.922g of NaCl into a 50 ml Falcon tube, then made up to 50 ml with MilliPore water A 50 mM TBS stock was created by adding 750 μl 1M NaCl solution to a 15 ml Falcon tube, then made up to 15 ml using Qiagen Elution Buffer (EB, i.e. 10 mM Tris-HCl at pH 8.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M NaCl stock
steps.instruction: Add 2.922 g NaCl to a 50 mL Falcon tube and bring the volume to 50 mL with Milli‑Pore water to make a 1 M NaCl solution.

steps.title: Make 50 mM TBS buffer
steps.instruction: Transfer 750 µL of the 1 M NaCl stock to a 15 mL Falcon tube, then add Qiagen Elution Buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl, pH 8.0) up to 15 mL to obtain 50 mM TBS; confirm pH 7.9–8.1 with a pH‑indicator strip.

steps.title: End‑prep reaction
steps.instruction: In a 1.5 mL LoBind tube, combine 10 µL (0.1 µg/µL) DNA ladder (1 µg total) with 33.5 µL TBS to a total volume of 43.5 µL, add 3.5 µL Ultra II End‑prep Reaction Buffer and 3 µL Ultra II End‑prep Enzyme Mix, mix gently, incubate 5 min at room temperature then 5 min at 65 °C.

steps.title: First bead cleanup
steps.instruction: Add 60 µL Ampure XP beads to the end‑prep reaction, rotate 5 min at room temperature, place on a magnetic rack, remove clear supernatant, wash beads twice with 150 µL 80 % ethanol, air‑dry 30 s, and elute DNA in 60 µL TBS.

steps.title: Adapter ligation
steps.instruction: To the eluate add 25 µL ONT Ligation Buffer (LNB), 5 µL NEBNext Quick T4 DNA Ligase (reduced from 10 µL), and 5 µL ONT Ligation Adapter (LA); mix gently, spin 1–3 s, incubate 10 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Final bead cleanup
steps.instruction: Add 40 µL Ampure XP beads (use 100 µL for Flongle samples), rotate 5 min at room temperature, magnetically separate, discard supernatant, wash beads twice with 250 µL ONT Long Fragment Buffer (LFB) for P2 Solo or 250 µL ONT Short Fragment Buffer (SFB) for Flongle, dry 30 s, then elute for 10 min at 37 °C in 15 µL ONT Elution Buffer (EB).

steps.title: Prepare flow cell flush
steps.instruction: Mix ONT Flow Cell Flush (FCF) with ONT Flow Cell Tether (FCT): for P2 Solo use 500 µL of a 1170 µL FCF solution containing 30 µL FCT; for Flongle use 60 µL of a 117 µL FCF solution containing 3 µL FCT, then flush the flow cell.

steps.title: Quantify and dilute library
steps.instruction: Measure 1 µL of the eluted library on a Quantus Fluorometer, transfer ~50 fmol (assuming 1 kb average length) to a new 1.5 µL tube; top up to 32 µL TBS for P2 Solo or 12 µL TBS for Flongle.

steps.title: Add sequencing buffers and beads
steps.instruction: To the diluted library add ONT Sequencing Buffer (SB) and ONT Library Beads (LIB): P2 Solo – 100 µL SB and 68 µL LIB; Flongle – 30 µL SB and 20 µL LIB.

steps.title: Load library onto flow cell
steps.instruction: Re‑flush the flow cell with an additional FCF/FCT mixture (500 µL for P2 Solo, 30 µL for Flongle), then add the sequencing library (200 µL for P2 Solo, 30 µL for Flongle) and let the flow cell sit 10 min before starting sequencing.

steps.title: Run sequencing and basecall
steps.instruction: Start MinKNOW v23.04.6 in fast mode (400 bases s⁻¹, minimum read length 20 bp, 5 kHz sampling) with POD5 output; run Flongle for 24 h, run P2 Solo (PromethION) for 1.5 h (stop after ≥200 reads ≥15 kb). Basecall reads with Dorado v0.4.0 using the 2023‑09‑22 bacterial methylation model.

steps.title: Assemble bands ≥3 kb
steps.instruction: Filter reads with quality >Q20 to a 100‑bp window around the target length (e.g., 4950‑5050 bp for a 5 kb band; use all reads for the 15 kb band). Chop reads into overlapping fragments with 1000 bp overlap (e.g., 3000 bp for the 5 kb band). Assemble with Canu v2.2 treating reads as PacBio, set GenomeSize to the expected band length (e.g., GenomeSize=5000). Extract the first contig, map it to nanopore adapter sequences, and trim any adapter matches. (Note: Canu defaults to 1 kb genome size and read‑length cutoff, performing poorly on shorter sequences.)

steps.title: Assemble bands <3 kb
steps.instruction: Filter reads >Q20 to a 100‑bp window around the target length (use all reads when high‑quality reads are insufficient, e.g., for the 100 bp band). Assemble with a k‑mer‑based de Bruijn assembler, trimming low‑count k‑mers; extract the first trimmed assembled chain, map to nanopore adapters, trim matching sequence, and use web BLASTn to remove any additional trailing non‑matching sequence.

steps.title: Map reads to assembled ladders
steps.instruction:
Create a LAST mismatch matrix with `last-train -Q 1 ladder_seqs.fa 5k_reads.fq.gz`. Map all reads to the assembled ladder sequences, retaining for each read the alignment with the longest combined proportion of read and reference mapped using the pipeline:
```
lastal -p bacterial.mat -P 10 ladder_seqs.fa reads_2023-Oct-12_DNA-Ladder-1kbplus_called_all.fq.gz \
  | ~/scripts/maf2csv.pl \
  | awk -F ',' '{print $0","($8/100 * $13/100)}' \
  | sort -t ',' -k 16rg,16 \
  | sort -t ',' -k 1,1 -u \
  | sort -t ',' -k 1r,1 \
  | perl -pe 's/,[^,]*$/\n/' \
  > LAST_reads_vs_ladder_longestMatch.csv.gz
```
